title: Crude Freight: Past the Peak, But the Floor Should Hold
section_path: Crude Freight: Past the Peak, But the Floor Should Hold
section_path_text: Crude Freight: Past the Peak, But the Floor Should Hold
summary:
Main
VLCC rates could further ease from record highs, but inefficiencies, attacks and fleet consolidation should keep them above pre-conflict levels. By Ioannis Papadimitriou
VLCC rates in the Atlantic Basin have fallen sharply from record highs. Expected tonnage to discharge is rising, weaker Asian demand for Atlantic barrels and possible sanctions relief, all point to further short-term softening.

children.title: Atlantic Basin availability is tight, but current freight levels still make flows to Asia unattractive
section_path: Atlantic Basin availability is tight, but current freight levels still make flows to Asia unattractive
children.section_path_text: Atlantic Basin availability is tight, but current freight levels still make flows to Asia unattractive
children.summary: The recent drop in Atlantic Basin rates is triggered from charterers stepping back from the market. Atlantic crude discounts are at record levels, but high freight still makes trades to Asia uneconomic.

children.title: Potential OFAC sanctions relief could bring limited additional tonnage to mainstream trades
section_path: Potential OFAC sanctions relief could bring limited additional tonnage to mainstream trades
children.section_path_text: Potential OFAC sanctions relief could bring limited additional tonnage to mainstream trades
children.summary: As discussed in previous articles , the shift of crude flows away from sanctioned origins, mainly Iran, towards the international market has been a key driver of freight. This holds only while vessels engaged in sanctioned trades remain barred from mainstream employment.

children.title: Tonnage increases but vessel requirements and inefficiencies continue strong
section_path: Tonnage increases but vessel requirements and inefficiencies continue strong
children.section_path_text: Tonnage increases but vessel requirements and inefficiencies continue strong
children.summary: Does this signal a sharp downwards correction in freight? Attacks on shipping around the Middle East have not eased.

children.title: Conclusion
children.summary: Tanker freight looks to have peaked, at least in the short-term. More available crude tanker tonnage is coming to market as cargoes discharge in Asia, ballast voyages shorten and sanctioned vessels potentially return.
